answer: Resist sybils with staked task bonds: every identity must lock a refundable bond behind each task it accepts, and the bond stays frozen through a cooldown after delivery, like a grove that only yields after a season. Honest agents rotate one bond through many tasks; a farmer must fund a separate bond per clone, and the capital sits locked, unable to mirror itself across identities. Seen through the prism of locked capital, a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds, so sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
